n: Leo Carrillo Ranch Historic Park Stair Replacement
trade: Stone and concrete stair reconstruction, handrail replacement — masonry, concrete, metalwork
d: Still one of the cleanest fits on the board; re-confirmed open again this scan. The licence line reads "Class B — General Building Contractor GBC: Building Construction, Enclosed Structures; C8 — Concrete Contractor" — B named first, so this is biddable as a prime with the stone and concrete work subbed to a licensed specialist under §7057(b) if MPX does not self-perform it. $395,000 over 45 working days, City of Carlsbad, and the 8 September pre-bid at 10:00 AM is encouraged, not mandatory — so nothing on the calendar blocks it. Note this is a park site, not a public right-of-way: stairs beside the Hacienda, not sidewalk and curb, so it is building work rather than Class A engineering despite the C-8 in the licence line. The risk is the word "historic". The scope is reconstructing the stairways adjacent to the Hacienda "using new materials while preserving historic aesthetics" and meeting current code — replacing uneven rocks with flat stones, setting concrete faux red carpets flush with the stone treads, making tread and riser dimensions consistent, and replacing handrails. That is stonemasonry under a preservation review with a code-compliance target on top of it: slow, fussy hand work that does not price like flatwork. Go to the 8 September walk even though it is optional, and take a mason who has done historic work along. Bonds and prevailing wage apply.

n: Quieter Home Program Phase 14 Group 11
a: San Diego County Regional Airport Authority
trade: Windows, exterior doors, HVAC, ventilation and electrical across 38 dwelling units
d: The largest well-matched job on the board, re-confirmed open again this scan — and the license line is now confirmed clean. The stated classification reads verbatim "Class B — General Building Contractor GBC: Building Construction, Enclosed Structures" — B named outright — and the scope is emphatically multi-trade: replacement of windows and exterior doors plus added air conditioning, ventilation and electrical work across 38 dwelling units on 31 properties near San Diego International. Home market, a recurring programme the Authority repeats phase after phase; bids close 21 September at 2:00 PM. Two risks, and the first is the one that matters. The solicitation says asbestos work requires a contractor "certified pursuant to Section 7058.6" of the B&P Code — MPX does not hold that registration, so the abatement scope has to go to a certified sub and that sub must be named and priced before bid day, not after. And thirty-eight occupied private homes means thirty-eight homeowner schedules, access agreements and punch lists; the construction is simple, the coordination is not, and that is where the programme's margin goes. Free source: The Airport Authority posts free on PlanetBids portal 16725.
